docs.title: Deltares MkDocs Template
docs.text:
The Deltares MkDocs Template can be found on GitHub.

This template is based on the Material for MkDocs theme and provides a starting point for creating documentation sites with MkDocs.

The purpose of this template is to provide a consistent look and feel for documentation sites created by Deltares, by providing some style examples and configurations.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• Get started with MkDocs - Get started with the Deltares MkDocs Template.
  • Deltares style guide - Examples showing some Deltares styles.

docs.title: Create your site
docs.text:
The Deltares MkDocs template is a starting point for creating your own documentation site. It provides a basic structure and configuration that you can customize to fit your needs.

In this guide, we will walk you through the steps to customize your own documentation site using the Deltares MkDocs template.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3
  • pip

You also need Material for MkDocs installed in your Python environment. See Running your site locally for the setup commands.

docs.title: Configure mkdocs.yml
docs.text:
The mkdocs.yml file in the project root controls your site's name, theme, navigation, and Markdown features. Edit this file rather than files in the generated site directory, which are overwritten on each build.

YAML uses indentation to group settings. Use spaces, not tabs, and keep list items aligned. Update the existing sections rather than adding duplicate top-level keys such as theme or nav.

docs.title: Site name and URL
docs.text:
Start by replacing the demonstration site's details with your own:

site_name: My project documentation
site_url: https://deltares-research.github.io/my-project/
site_description: User and developer documentation for my project.
site_author: Deltares
Setting Purpose site_name The name displayed in the header and browser title. site_url The full public URL where the site will be published, including a project subpath when applicable. Keep the trailing slash. site_description An optional summary used in the site's HTML metadata. site_author Optional author metadata.

The URL above is an example; use your actual publishing location. Setting site_url does not deploy the site. See Deploy your site for publishing instructions.

docs.title: Keep the Deltares theme
docs.text:
This project uses Material for MkDocs with local Deltares template overrides. Keep the following settings to retain the Deltares layout, logo, and colours:

theme:
  name: material
  custom_dir: deltares/overrides
  logo: assets/logo-of-deltares.svg
  favicon: assets/favicon-16x16.png
  language: en
  palette:
    - scheme: default
      primary: custom
      accent: custom

custom_dir is relative to the directory containing mkdocs.yml. It loads the templates and assets from deltares/overrides, including the Deltares stylesheet through main.html. Keep that directory when reusing this configuration in another project; installing Material alone does not provide these overrides.

The logo and favicon paths refer to site assets. The supplied files are in deltares/overrides/assets. To use your own images, place them in an assets directory under docs and change logo and favicon to their paths relative to docs, for example assets/my-project-logo.svg.

language controls the theme's interface labels, not the language of your Markdown content. For Dutch interface labels, use language: nl.

docs.title: Navigation and interface features
docs.text:
The features list belongs inside the existing theme section:

theme:
  # Keep the other theme settings here.
  features:
    - navigation.tabs
    - navigation.tabs.sticky
    - navigation.expand
    - navigation.path
    - navigation.top
    - navigation.footer
    - search.suggest
    - search.highlight
    - content.code.copy
    - toc.integrate
Feature Effect navigation.tabs Shows top-level navigation sections as tabs on larger screens. navigation.tabs.sticky Keeps navigation tabs visible while scrolling. navigation.expand Expands navigation sections by default. navigation.path Enables breadcrumb navigation in Material versions that support it. navigation.top Adds a back-to-top button. navigation.footer Shows previous and next page links in the footer. search.suggest Enables search suggestions. search.highlight Highlights matching search terms on destination pages. content.code.copy Adds copy buttons to code blocks. toc.integrate Places the page's table of contents in the left navigation instead of a separate sidebar.

Remove a feature's list entry to disable it. Do not leave an empty - entry. Feature availability can depend on your installed Material version; consult the Material setup documentation when choosing additional features.

docs.title: Organize pages with nav
docs.text:
Use the top-level nav section to choose page labels, order, and grouping. For example, the following uses pages already included in this project:

nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - Get started:
      - MkDocs: mkdocs/mkdocs.md
      - Create your site: mkdocs/create_your_site.md
      - Deploy your site: mkdocs/deploy_your_site.md
  - Deltares styles:
      - Buttons: style_examples/buttons.md
      - Headers: style_examples/headers.md
      - Lists: style_examples/lists.md
      - Tables: style_examples/tables.md

Page paths are relative to docs by default, not to mkdocs.yml. For example, to add a user guide, create user_guide.md inside docs, then add - User guide: user_guide.md at the desired position in nav. The label before the colon controls the menu text; the page's Markdown heading controls its visible heading.

With navigation.tabs enabled, top-level groups such as Get started become tabs. Nested entries form their navigation menus. Removing a page from nav does not delete it or prevent MkDocs from building it.

docs.title: Enable Markdown features
docs.text:
The top-level markdown_extensions section enables syntax used by the example pages:

markdown_extensions:
  - attr_list
  - pymdownx.emoji:
      emoji_index: !!python/name:material.extensions.emoji.twemoji
      emoji_generator: !!python/name:material.extensions.emoji.to_svg
  - def_list
  - pymdownx.tasklist:
      custom_checkbox: true
  - tables
  - pymdownx.superfences
  - pymdownx.tabbed:
      alternate_style: true

attr_list supports attributes such as the CSS classes used for buttons. The other entries enable emoji and icons, definition lists, task lists, tables, enhanced fenced code blocks, and content tabs. Keep the extensions required by your pages. The extensions shown here are available with the Material for MkDocs installation.

docs.title: Add project-specific CSS or JavaScript
docs.text:
The project includes optional files in docs/stylesheets/extra.css and docs/javascripts/extra.js. Enable them by uncommenting the corresponding settings in mkdocs.yml:

extra_css:
  - stylesheets/extra.css
extra_javascript:
  - javascripts/extra.js

These are top-level settings, not entries under theme. Paths are relative to docs. Use these files for project-specific additions rather than modifying Material's installed files. The Deltares stylesheet is already loaded by the template override; it does not need an extra_css entry.

docs.title: Preview your configuration
docs.text:
From the project root, with your Python environment activated, run:

python -m mkdocs serve

Open the local URL printed in the terminal. Save mkdocs.yml or a Markdown page to rebuild the preview automatically. Check the site title, navigation, images, and any Markdown features you use. If MkDocs reports an error, check YAML indentation and confirm that referenced pages and assets exist.

Before publishing, build the static site:

python -m mkdocs build

For additional settings, see the MkDocs configuration reference and the Material for MkDocs documentation.

docs.title: Publishing your site
docs.text:
Detailed instructions on how to publish your site can be found in the MkDocs documentation.

And more specifically, the Material for MkDocs documentation provides instructions on how to deploy your site to different platforms.

docs.title: Running your site locally
docs.text:
Run these commands from the project root, where mkdocs.yml is located. First, create and activate a Python virtual environment, then install Material for MkDocs (which includes MkDocs):

python -m venv .venv

Activate the environment:

# Windows PowerShell
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# macOS or Linux
source .venv/bin/activate

Install the project dependencies:

python -m pip install mkdocs-material

Build the site into the site/ directory:

mkdocs build

To preview the site locally, start MkDocs' development server:

mkdocs serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ in your browser. The server rebuilds the site when you save documentation changes; stop it with Ctrl+C.

docs.title: Publishing your site
docs.text:
There are different ways to publish your site, depending on the platform you want to use. The most common platforms are GitHub Pages and GitLab Pages.

On the Material for MkDocs documentation you can find instructions on how to deploy your site to different platforms.

Here are some specific instructions for publishing to one of the Deltares supported platforms.

mkdocs gh-deploy --force

docs.title: Deltares supported Pages
docs.text: Deltares offers a number of hosting locations for your documentation site.

docs.title: GitHub
docs.text:
GitHub specific instructions for deploying your site can be found in the GitHub Pages documentation.

The following GitHub pages locations are available for hosting your documentation site:

  • Deltares GitHub Pages - for public documentation sites for the Deltares organization.
  • Deltares Research GitHub Pages - for documentation sites of the Deltares Research organization.

docs.title: GitLab
docs.text:
GitLab specific instructions for deploying your site can be found in the GitLab Pages documentation.

Currently, Deltares does not offer GitLab Pages hosting for documentation sites. However, we are working on providing this in the neer future.

The expected GitLab Pages hosting locations for Deltares documentation sites are:

  • Deltares GitLab Pages - for public documentation sites hosted in the Deltares GitLab instance.
  • Open Deltares GitLab Pages - for public documentation sites hosted in the Open Deltares GitLab instance.

docs.title: MkDocs
docs.text: MkDocs is a static site generator that's geared towards building project documentation. It takes Markdown files and builds a static HTML website from them.

docs.title: Material for MkDocs
docs.text: Material for MkDocs is a theme for MkDocs that provides a modern and responsive design, along with many features and customization options. It is widely used in the MkDocs community and is known for its clean and professional look.

docs.title: Deltares MkDocs Template
docs.text: The Deltares MkDocs Template is an adaptation of the Material for MkDocs theme. It provides stylesheet customizations that offer users a simple way to design project documentation that is consistent in look and feel with Deltares.

docs.title: Markdown Buttons
docs.text:
Markdown does not offer a simple way to create buttons. However the squidfunk mkdocs project does.

Through the deltares.css stylesheet it is possible to style these buttons.

The current styles defined in the deltares.css file are configured according to the Deltares design guidelines.

The entries for the Button styles are can be found in the deltares.css under section:

 /* Deltares overrides for Buttons */

docs.title: Simple Button
docs.text:
Button

[Subscribe to our newsletter](#){ .md-button }
Subscribe to our newsletter

docs.title: Icon Button
docs.text:
Button with icon

[:fontawesome-solid-arrow-right:](buttons.md){ .md-button }

docs.title: HTML Buttons
docs.text:
If you wish for more control over the styling of buttons, then it is possible to use HTML and CSS.

Below is an example of a button with an icon and text. The button is defined in the deltares.css file under section:

 /* Deltares overrides for Buttons */

docs.title: Goto Button (HTML)
docs.text:
Goto Button

<div class="md-group__items"> 
  <div class="md-button md-group__item__button">
    <a  href="#">
        <img alt="arrow right" width="20" height="20"  src="../../assets/arrow-right.svg">
    </a>
  </div>
  <div class="md-group__item__text">
    <a href="#" >
        <h4>Goto</h4>
    </a>
  </div>
</div>
`

Goto

docs.title: Markdown Headers
docs.text:
Markdown offers a simple way to create headers. Documentation can be found here.

# Header style 1
## Header style 2
### Header style 3
#### Header style 4
##### Header style 5
###### Header style 6

Through the deltares.css stylesheet it is possible to style the headers.

The current styles defined in the deltares.css file are configured according to the Deltares design guidelines.

The entries for the Header styles are can be found in the deltares.css under section:

 /* Deltares overrides for Headers */

docs.title: Markdown Lists
docs.text:
Markdown offers a simple way to create lists as is shown in the Markdown list reference.

For a more complex reference specifically designed for MkDocs, please refer to the reference in Material for MkDocs.

Through the deltares.css stylesheet it is possible to style these lists.

The current styles defined in the deltares.css file are configured according to the Deltares design guidelines.

The entries for the List styles are can be found in the deltares.css under section:

 /* Deltares overrides for Lists */

docs.title: Unordered List
docs.text:
Markdown Unordered List
* First item
* Second item
* Third item
____- Subitem 1
____- Subitem 2
________+ Subsubitem 1
________+ Subsubitem 2
  • First item
  • Second item
  • Third item
    • Subitem 1
    • Subitem 2
      • Subsubitem 1
      • Subsubitem 2

docs.title: Ordered List
docs.text:
Markdown Ordered List
1. First item

    ```Add an image.``` ![Deltares logo](./assets/favicon-16x16.png)

2. Second item

    ```Add a code block here to show that the list is still active.```

3. Third item
    1. Subitem 1
    2. Subitem 2
        1. Subsubitem 1
        2. Subsubitem 2

  1. First item

    Add an image.

  2. Second item

    Add a code block here to show that the list is still active.

  3. Third item

    1. Subitem 1
    2. Subitem 2
      1. Subsubitem 1
      2. Subsubitem 2

docs.title: HTML List
docs.text:
If you wish for more control over the styling of lists, then it is possible to use HTML and CSS.

The CSS entries for styling the HTML lists are defined in the same section of the deltares.css file as the Markdown lists.:

 /* Deltares overrides for Lists */
HTML Ordered List
<div class="md-typeset__list">
    <ol>
        <li>First item</li>
        <li>Second item</li>
        <li>Third item
            <ol class="md">
                <li>Subitem 1</li>
                <li>Subitem 2
                    <ol>
                        <li>Subsubitem 1</li>
                        <li>Subsubitem 2</li>
                    </ol>
                </li>
            </ol>
        </li>
    </ol>
</div>
  1. First item
  2. Second item
  3. Third item
    1. Subitem 1
    2. Subitem 2
      1. Subsubitem 1
      2. Subsubitem 2

docs.title: Markdown Tables
docs.text:
Markdown offers a simple way to create tables as is shown in the Markdown table reference. More elaborate Table styling options specifically for MkDocs can be found in the squidfunk mkdocs project.

Through the deltares.css stylesheet it is possible to style these tables.

The current styles defined in the deltares.css file are configured according to the Deltares design guidelines.

The entries for the Table styles are can be found in the deltares.css under section:

 /* Deltares overrides for Tables */
Markdown Table
| Chart Title      | Euro x1000|Index|
| :----------------| --------: |----:|
| Item 1           | XXX       |XXX  |
| Item 2           | XXX       | XXX |
| Item 3           | XXX       | XXX |
Chart Title Euro x1000 Index Item 1 XXX XXX Item 2 XXX XXX Item 3 XXX XXX

docs.title: HTML Tables
docs.text:
If you wish for more control over the styling of tables, then it is possible to use HTML and CSS.

Deltares supports two colour schemes for tables: Blue (class="md-typeset__table__blue") and Green (class="md-typeset__table__green").

The definitions for these table styles are defined in the deltares.css file under section:

 /* Deltares overrides for Tables */
BlueGreen HTML Table definition
    <table class="md-typeset__table__blue">
        <tr >
          <th align="left">Chart Title</th>
          <th align="right">Euro x1000</th>
          <th align="right">Index</th>
        </tr>
        <tr >
          <td align="left">Item 1</td>
          <td align="right">XXX</td>
          <td align="right">XXX</td>
        </tr>
        <tr >
          <td align="left">Item 2</td>
          <td align="right">XXX</td>
          <td align="right">XXX</td>
        </tr>
        <tr >
          <td align="left"><strong>Item 3</strong></td>
          <td align="right"><strong>XXX</strong></td>
          <td align="right"><strong>XXX</strong></td>
        </tr>
    </table>

Chart Title Euro x1000 Index Item 1 XXX XXX Item 2 XXX XXX Item 3 XXX XXX
